parts.text: Which claim about starting and continuing burning is best?

options.text: Burning needs fuel, oxygen, and enough heat to reach ignition temperature; under the glass the oxygen runs low, and wet paper needs more heating to reach ignition.
Once lit, the candle needs only wax as fuel; oxygen and heat above ignition temperature are not needed for continued burning.
Wet paper fails to catch fire because paper is never a fuel, wet or dry.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

stem: Wasim lights a candle. It burns steadily. He then covers the candle with a glass. After some time the flame goes out. He also finds that a wet paper strip does not catch fire from the same match as quickly as a dry paper strip.

part_answers.answer: Combustion continues only while fuel, oxygen, and heat above ignition temperature are all present; covering cuts oxygen, and wet paper is harder to heat to ignition.

teacher.key_rationale: Combustion needs fuel, oxygen, and enough heat to reach ignition temperature. Covering the candle limits oxygen; wet paper needs more heat to reach ignition than dry paper.
